 Wales v New Zealand (14:10 GMT)
 Wales have not beaten the All Blacks since 1953
 Wales make four starting changes from the victory over Japan in Cardiff
 Taine Basham makes his first Wales Test start since 2022
 New Zealand have made eight starting changes from the side that defeated Scotland at Murrayfield
 Full-back Beauden Barrett will captain New Zealand for the first time

 Wales face the Haka published at 14:08 GMT 14:08 GMT 
 Wales v New Zealand (14:10 GMT) 
 Lights were wheeled onto the pitch after the anthems and placed behind the Wales players as they faced the Haka.
 A spotlight went on the New Zealand players, with lights from mobile phones filling the stands.
 Red lights were shone behind Dewi Lake and his team as they lined up on the 10-metre line.
 Now we're almost ready for the off...

 The man in the middle published at 14:02 GMT 14:02 GMT 
 Wales v New Zealand (14:10 GMT) 
 Image source, Huw French referee Pierre Brousset is in charge this afternoon, with Australia's Nic Berry and France's Luc Ramos his assistants.
 Fingers crossed we won't hear too much from TMO Tual Trainini.
 Brousset refereed England's win against Australia on Sunday and was last in charge of a Wales game earlier this year, also at Twickenham.
 Nicky Smith, Dewi Lake, Ben Thomas and Taine Plumtree were all shown yellow cards in a horrendous Six Nations opener.

 Wary of Wales published at 14:00 GMT 14:00 GMT 
 Wales v New Zealand (14:10 GMT) 
 Image source, Huw Evans Picture Agency New Zealand are hot favourites but they insist there is no danger of complacency.
 Boss Dave Rennie, formerly head coach at Glasgow, was quick to praise Welsh talent on Thursday.
 "In Tomos Williams, they have one of the best nines in the world," he said.
 "We've got to make sure we don't let him have too much space, because he's got such a high-quality kicking game and kicks off both feet.
 "They've got a number of players that if we give them time and space, they'll be a handful.
 "They have a big midfield and absolute jets on the wing, so we know a fair bit about the enemy."

 Flashback: Rogers makes history published at 13:52 GMT 13:52 GMT 
 Wales v New Zealand (14:10 GMT) 
 Image source, Huw Evans Picture Agency Wales need to put in a big performance to keep things tight, as they did for much of last year's meeting between the sides.
 New Zealand led just 24-21 early in the second half before stretching away to win convincingly 52-26 .
 Wales did cross the line four times last November - which would earn a bonus point today - through their wings.
 Louis Rees-Zammit produced an acrobatic finish in the right corner in the first half while Tom Rogers went over three times down the left.
 Rogers, who has switched from Scarlets to Ospreys to try and focus on being a full-back, became the first Welsh player to score a hat-trick against New Zealand.

 Wales' list of misery published at 13:45 GMT 13:45 GMT 
 Wales v New Zealand (14:10 GMT) 
 Image source, Huw Evans Picture Agency Wales won the first meeting with New Zealand on 16 December, 1905 and enjoyed a 13-8 triumph on 19 December, 1953.
 It has been nothing but misery since with 34 straight losses.
 The infamous Andy Haden dive in 1978 is sixth in the list, Andrew Hore's punch at 25 and the thriller under Mike Ruddock in 2004 at 17.

 Gabriel's great opportunity published at 13:42 GMT 13:42 GMT 
 Wales v New Zealand (14:10 GMT) 
 Image source, Huw Evans Picture Agency Josh Adams played well when scoring a double against Japan a week ago but the veteran is given a breather.
 That presents a chance for in-form Leicester wing Gabriel Hamer-Webb, who gets the nod ahead of Ellis Mee and Macs Page.
 The 26-year-old wins his second cap after a tough time against Scotland in the Six Nations in February.
 Former Cardiff back Hamer-Webb has been sharp for Prem leaders Leicester.
 "Some players would probably shy away from what the game was but you didn't even need to go through it with him he knew, exactly what it was and he's aligned to it," said Tandy.
 "You look at the way he's gone to Leicester, with guys like Adam Radwan and Ollie Hassell-Collins in fine form, and he's broken into that.
 "So I think he deserves this opportunity."

 All Blacks impress in Edinburgh published at 13:39 GMT 13:39 GMT 
 Wales v New Zealand (14:10 GMT) 
 Image source, PA Media New Zealand spent the start of the week preparing in Bath after getting off to a winning start in Scotland.
 The All Blacks produced an impressive second-half performance to blow away the Scots, turning a 24-21 half-time lead into a 43-21 success.
 Wales must avoid the poor discipline that proved to be Scotland's downfall.
 "Whether it was an offside, or an error around the breakdown, we were getting penalised and put into our 22," admitted Gregor Townsend.
 "Against New Zealand, who came out with innovation and power, it is hard to stop them with modern laws. You've got to keep them out your 22 and we didn't do that enough."

 Eyes on the crowd published at 13:33 GMT 13:33 GMT 
 Wales v New Zealand (14:10 GMT) 
 Image source, Huw Evans Picture Agency In recent years it would have been unthinkable for tickets to be available on matchday for this fixture.
 Yet there is the very real possibility of there being several thousand empty seats at Principality Stadium.
 That is a reflection of the one-sided rivalry and the off-field turmoil that continues to sap energy.
 It looks likely that this afternoon's attendance will be the smallest for a New Zealand fixture at Principality Stadium, although a crowd in the 60,000s is still not to be sniffed at.
 Nonetheless, the All Blacks are relishing the occasion.
 "I don't know what it is about this place, maybe it's about
the people that make it," said captain Beauden Barrett.
 "The passion, the pride that comes with Welsh rugby and
the supporters, obviously the singing.
 "A closed arena, something so grand
like this, there's a lot of great things to talk about."
 Hopefully Wales will give the punters plenty to cheer.
 The WRU have been copping plenty of flak of late but you do have to feel for them when it comes to next weekend.
 The Australia game kicks off at 20:10 GMT, which is certainly not friendly for families and will make using public transport a nightmare for those in Cardiff, let alone those going further afield.

 Brilliant Barrett leads the way published at 13:30 GMT 13:30 GMT 
 Wales v New Zealand (14:10 GMT) 
 Image source, Huw Evans Picture Agency Beauden Barrett scored twice against Scotland to bring up a half-century of tries for the All Blacks.
 The full-back remains a class act and will aim to add to his eight scores against Wales this afternoon.
 Not only will Barrett be a key figure with ball in hand but he's leading New Zealand for the first time in a Test.
 “I’ve had the honour before in a game against the Baa-Baas at
Twickenham but doing it in a Test match at a stadium like this, against a proud
nation in Wales, is a great opportunity," he said ahead of his 149th cap.
 “I'm not going to try and do anything that I haven't
already. It's about having that relationship with a referee.
 “From 15 there’s a bit of distance there and I might be
doing a few more extra shuttles, but I’ve got great support around me.”
 Barrett's experience will be vital given the changes that the All Blacks have made to the starting line-up.
 "All of those players are chomping at the bit to get out
there," he said.
 "It's been a week of working on new combinations, but with that comes
a lot of excitement."

 Captain Lake not thinking about history published at 13:27 GMT 13:27 GMT 
 Wales v New Zealand (14:10 GMT) 
 Dewi Lake was born in May 1999, so has only been alive for 21 of Wales' defeats by New Zealand. 
 Four of them have come after his Ospreys debut in 2018.
 Lake has beaten New Zealand as a member of the 2019 Wales side at the World Rugby U20 Championships, but is not thinking of the past or making history.

 Wales arrive published at 13:21 GMT 13:21 GMT 
 Wales v New Zealand (14:10 GMT) 
 It the second of three games at Principality Stadium for Wales in the Nations Championship, with a trip over the Severn Bridge for finals weekend at Twickenham at the end of the month.
 Steve Tandy's men will have been inspired by the crowds on Westgate Street as they made it to the ground.

 All Blacks tinker before Twickenham published at 13:18 GMT 13:18 GMT 
 Wales v New Zealand (14:10 GMT) 
 Image source, Huw Evans Picture Agency Beauden Barrett captains New Zealand from full-back when winning his 149th cap.
 The All Blacks make eight changes to the starting line-up that beat Scotland 43-21, perhaps with one eye on England next weekend.
 Flanker Anton Segner and wing Fehi Fineanganofo make their first Test starts.
 Segner, prop George Bower, hooker Asafo Aumua and scrum-half Cortez Ratima move from the replacements into the starting side.
 Fly-half Richie Mo'unga (pictured) , Fineanganofo, lock Josh Lord and centre Anton Lienert-Brown also come into the XV.
 "We have created good depth in this group and there is a lot of competition for places," said Rennie.
 New Zealand: B Barrett (capt); Fineanganofo, Tupaea, Lienert-Brown, Moorby; Mo'unga, Ratima; Bower, Aumua, Newell, S Barrett, Lord, Segner, Lakai, Sititi.
 Replacements: Bell, Numia, Tosi, Hannah, E Blackadder, Fainga'anuku, Preston, R Ioane.

 Basham's big chance published at 13:13 GMT 13:13 GMT 
 Wales v New Zealand (14:10 GMT) 
 Image source, Huw Evans Picture Agency Wales have suffered a blow with the loss of number eight Aaron Wainwright through injury.
 The Leicester forward's absence presents a chance for his former Dragons team-mate Taine Basham to take his Cardiff club form onto the international stage.
 It is his first Wales start since 2022 and he will hope to repeat his dynamic display against the All Blacks in November 2021.
 James Botham replaces Alex Mann at blind-side flanker and wing Josh Adams is rested, with Gabriel Hamer-Webb coming into the side for his second cap.
 The fourth change to the XV sees lock Adam Beard get the nod ahead of Ben Carter.
 Back rower Taine Plumtree and props Gareth Thomas and Dillon Lewis are named among the replacements.
 Wales: Murray; Rees-Zammit, E James, Llewellyn, Hamer-Webb; Costelow, Tomos Williams; N Smith, Lake (capt), Griffin, D Jenkins, Beard, Botham, Morgan Basham.
 Replacements: Elias, G Thomas, D Lewis, Carter, Plumtree, Morgan-Williams, Edwards, Hennessey.
